name: Bookings and reservations (the operator's capacity diary)
one_line: Who is coming, when, for how many, and with what requirements — the OPERATOR's reservation book, diary, PMS or covers export, the confirmation that answers a dated demand against finite capacity, the deposit or guarantee note that binds it, and the cancellation or no-show record that closes it. Recognised by a CAPACITY-AGAINST-DATED-DEMAND structure carrying a STATUS slot and usually a REQUIREMENTS slot, held as a POPULATION or a CYCLE on the operator's side — never by the words booking, reservation or confirmation alone, and never by a single customer-addressed voucher sitting in Downloads beside boarding passes. A PLACEHOLDER TEMPLATE: it writes NO field rows and recommends NO folder dimensions, because the retail_hospitality schema declares none (PR-6, D1 as narrowed).

deterministic: PRECONDITION on every entry below: each is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The schema declares no field rows, so nothing here writes a domain fact. Detection exists so the material is recognised, kept local where this row's sensitivity says so, and offered honestly. The ordinary contents of this row are third-party personal data about guests. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

A CAPACITY-AGAINST-DATED-DEMAND structure WITH A STATUS SLOT. A finite capacity — covers, pax, party size, guest count, room-nights, table or seat allocation, ticket count — is bound to a date and a time window, with a labelled status drawn from a short reservation vocabulary (confirmed, provisional, held, cancelled, no-show, arrived, seated, checked-in, checked-out). A calendar entry with attendees is NOT this; the discriminator is the counted quantity against a stated or implied capacity plus a reservation-status slot. “Calendar formats such as ICS should yield event title, start and end time, location, organizer, attendees, and recurrence metadata.” Where the evidence is an ICS file the CONTENT is what fires; source_type = calendar contributes only as a file-kind signal.

A REQUIREMENTS OR SPECIAL-REQUESTS structure co-located with the capacity demand: dietary and allergen notes, accessibility requests, cot or extra bed, late checkout, connecting rooms, celebration notes, seating preference, or a named product or room type allocated to the occasion. The requirements block is operator operational apparatus; a customer voucher that only restates the date and the party size without a requirements or status apparatus is not this row's strongest form.

A POPULATION DIARY OR BOOKING-BOOK EXPORT. A tabular record with one row per dated occasion across a service, a trading day, a house, or a channel — booking reference, party size or room-nights, time window, status, and often a guest contact or name column — produced by a PMS, a reservation book, an OpenTable or similar diary export, or a covers sheet. The population is the discriminator against a single transactional confirmation: many occasions, one site, one period.

A RESERVATION-LIFECYCLE CHAIN read across several files or several messages sharing one booking reference: inquiry or hold → provisional or confirmed confirmation → deposit or guarantee request → amendment → cancellation or no-show note. The chain, not any one member, is the signal; an isolated confirmation email without a recurring reference beside other members is weak.

A DEPOSIT, GUARANTEE OR PREPAYMENT INSTRUMENT whose labelled slots name a booking or reservation reference, an occasion date, and a capacity or product allocation — not merely an amount and a merchant. Money alone never fires; the reference-plus-occasion pairing does. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

A WAITLIST OR REALLOCATION STRUCTURE: ranked requests against a full service or sold-out date, with party size, preferred time, contact, and a promoted-or-released status. The capacity constraint is explicit; a generic CRM lead list is not this structure.

An email whose labelled subject slot names a booking or reservation reference together with a covers, party-size, room-night or date token, AND whose body or attachment carries confirmation, amendment, cancellation or deposit language. The reference-plus-quantity pairing is what fires; a hospitality-sounding sender domain alone does not.

A scan or photograph of a paper reservation book page, a handwritten covers sheet, or a printed PMS screen — a grid of times against tables or rooms, party sizes, and initials. “A screenshot is always a screenshot of something—a receipt, application portal, conversation, code problem, document, calendar, or research figure—and without OCR the product sees only an image with a weak filename.”

An archive whose MANIFEST names a night's reservations, a PMS export, a covers diary, a booking period dump or a channel reservation download — read from the manifest alone, because “However, the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem, because doing so creates security, storage, and side-effect risks.”

Parent-folder context naming reservations, bookings, diary, covers, PMS, front office or a trading date, treated as a clue that raises plausibility once one of the structures above is already present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this row's ordinary output names members of the public, their contact details, dietary needs and sometimes payment-guarantee tokens. A model step runs under the user's policy and after P7. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

WHOSE SIDE IS THIS — the row's central determination and the one inherited most sharply from the schema. A booking confirmation, a hotel voucher and a restaurant reservation each exist twice: once as the operator's record (here) and once as the guest's (travel.bookings-confirmations on finance, or the Receipts and Confirmations residual). Filenames are often identical and both are PDFs. The operator's copy carries a POPULATION, a STATUS apparatus, a REQUIREMENTS block managed by the house, or a recurring reference inside an operator export; the guest's copy carries exactly one transaction addressed to the holder as diner or traveller. Where evidence does not settle which side the holder is on, this row must not activate.

Separating a LIVE reservation record from a TEMPLATE, a PMS vendor's sample export, a training diary, a franchise specimen confirmation, or a blank booking form. A blank covers sheet and a completed one are the same grid with the names removed. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”

A purpose-coherent booking packet whose members are individually unremarkable: the confirmation PDF, a deposit receipt, a dietary email, a table-plan image and a cancellation note sharing one reference. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

Unlabelled operational prose — a host's handwritten note that table 12 is holding for eight, a WhatsApp screenshot about a late party, a shift handover listing expected covers. These often lack a header block and are among the most sensitive files because they name guests and staff together.
Reading handwriting on a photographed reservation book, where OCR confidence is low and the guest contact column is frequently the most legible thing on the page.
A reservation record in a language whose hospitality, covers, room-night and cancellation vocabulary the deterministic structure catalogue does not cover.

Whether a dated function confirmation is this row's reservation of the date or retail_hospitality.event-production's production of the day — settled by whether the artefact is capacity-and-status apparatus or minute-keyed delivery apparatus; abstain when both are absent. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
In every case above, abstention is the required outcome when evidence does not settle it.
never_alone: THE WORDS `booking`, `reservation`, `confirmation`, `diary`, `covers`, `guest`, `table`, `room` OR `hotel`, STANDING ALONE. The schema already forbids sector vocabulary as sole proof; this row sharpens it because those exact tokens are this world's filename default and also name travel vouchers, medical appointments, meeting invites, software holds and Residual `Receipts and Confirmations` material. `Booking.pdf` is nothing. What fires is capacity-against-dated-demand with status, a population diary, or a reservation-lifecycle chain — never the word.

A TRADE NAME OR VENUE NAME, STANDING ALONE — `Le Petit Jardin`, `The Bell`, `Harbour Hotel`. Role ambiguity is the design floor: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” A venue name is worse, because it can be the holder's own site, a place the holder booked as a guest, a supplier, a competitor, or a cited example.

A GUEST'S, DINER'S OR LEAD-NAME. This is the row's hardest rule. The guest name is the most salient token on almost every artefact this row holds, and it must never anchor a group and must never become a folder level: the design warns when a level “creates a large number of tiny folders”, and a branch per diner is the purest instance — as well as publishing a member of the public into the directory tree.

A SHORT ALPHANUMERIC STRING that resembles a booking reference. It can equally be an order, invoice, case, ticket, medical appointment or event identifier unless a labelled reservation slot or capacity-status structure gives it a role.
A DATE OR DATE-AND-TIME, STANDING ALONE, however hospitality-shaped. Nearly every file in this world is dated; a date identifies an occasion only inside a capacity-and-status structure.

A CURRENCY AMOUNT, DEPOSIT FIGURE OR CARD-TAIL, STANDING ALONE. The same evidence supports an ordinary receipt, invoice or account record and must be resolved by the reservation reference and occasion slots, not by money.
A PARTY SIZE OR COVER COUNT, STANDING ALONE. Eight people appear on meeting invites, clinical group sessions, coach bookings and catering proposals alike.
source_type or extension alone, including text_document, spreadsheet, email, calendar, image, ocr, archive, .pdf, .xlsx, .csv, .eml, .ics, .png or .zip. File kind is routing evidence only.

Membership in a download, email or travel-planning session. A session can retrieve neighbours but is not proof of topic or purpose — and the schema's own collision fixture sits in Downloads beside boarding passes precisely to prove that.

grouping_reasons: ONE BOOKING REFERENCE across its confirmation, deposit, requirements note, amendment and cancellation or no-show — purpose-coherent even where members share little content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
ONE TRADING DATE OR SERVICE at one site: the covers diary, the waitlist and the no-show log for one dinner or one house-night — joined by the occasion, never by a guest surname.
ONE CHANNEL EXPORT PERIOD: an OpenTable, Booking.com or PMS dump for one site over one bounded window, joined by the export's own period header rather than by individual guest names.

No group at all is a valid and COMMON outcome for an isolated guest-addressed confirmation. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.” That sentence names booking records explicitly.

template.why: EMPTY BY CONTRACT: PR-6 leaves the retail_hospitality schema with no field rows, and a dimension may only branch on a field the same schema declares. The recommendation is therefore held as prose, and it is stated here because the node test requires this row to say how it differs from the schema's default — which reads: the TRADING UNIT only where the corpus spans more than one, then the TRADING OCCASION (session, count, order cycle, booking, function, licensed activity), then the OPERATIONAL RECORD FUNCTION, not time-first. THIS ROW KEEPS THAT SHAPE and specialises the middle and trailing levels: site (conditional) → the BOOKING ITSELF as trading_occasion (the dated capacity demand identified by a reservation reference or a service-plus-time) → BOOKING RECORD FUNCTION (confirmation, deposit, amendment, cancellation, no-show, waitlist). Trading period sits INSIDE the occasion, never above the site. NOT TIME-FIRST: this row is more tempted than most because every artefact carries a stay or service date, and the answer is that the date IDENTIFIES the occasion rather than ROOTING the tree — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” — and the time-first licence belongs to capture-based media alone: “Photos and capture-based media are the major exception: time often belongs first because capture date is a defining aspect of the material.” A reservation is not a capture. TWO ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS bind harder here than on stocktake or POS siblings: a GUEST, DINER OR LEAD NAME must never become a dimension, and a BOOKING REFERENCE must not become a deep tree of one-child branches per code — the design warns against levels that create “a large number of tiny folders” and against using “an author or organization merely as a collector”. Any later order remains editable because “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.” Honest strain recorded as NJ-BR-1: because the occasion level IS the booking, this row's dimensional difference from the family default is thinner than guest-feedback's; the row survives on detection and privacy, not on a dramatic reorder.

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Booking confirmation - Le Petit Jardin 14 Mar.pdf` — restaurant name, date, time, party of four, booking reference, cancellation policy, addressed to the holder as diner and sitting in Downloads beside boarding passes (the retail_hospitality schema anchor's own collision fixture). THIS ROW OWNS the OPERATOR's copy: a population diary, PMS export, house-managed requirements apparatus, or confirmation retained inside the site's booking cycle. THAT ROW OWNS the TRAVELLER OR DINER's transactional voucher on the finance schema — issuer institution plus record_type for a journey or stay the holder is taking. Discriminated by HOLDER ROLE and APPARATUS: operator population or house status/requirements apparatus decides for this row; holder-as-guest with a single-transaction voucher and no operational diary decides for travel.bookings-confirmations. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.BOOKINGS-RESERVATIONS MUST NOT TAKE a guest's downloaded restaurant or hotel voucher merely because it says booking; TRAVEL.BOOKINGS-CONFIRMATIONS MUST NOT TAKE a PMS covers export merely because it contains reservation rows.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Ashcroft 06.06.26 - confirmation and deposit.pdf` — event date, covers, booking reference, deposit, named lead client (the reciprocal of the edge that row already authored). THIS ROW OWNS the RESERVATION OF THE DATE: capacity, status, deposit/guarantee and requirements that hold the occasion before or without delivery planning. THAT ROW OWNS the PRODUCTION OF THE DAY: minute-keyed run sheet, supplier call times, on-the-day log and post-event reconciliation. Discriminated by whether the artefact is capacity-and-status apparatus or clock-and-delivery apparatus. BOOKINGS-RESERVATIONS MUST NOT TAKE a run sheet merely because it names covers; EVENT-PRODUCTION MUST NOT TAKE a provisional hold-and-deposit confirmation merely because the occasion is a wedding.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Appointments_2026-03.csv` — named individuals, dates, time slots, durations, contact numbers, notes column; capacity-against-dated-demand on its face (the schema anchor's clinical seam). THIS ROW OWNS the slot that consumes FINITE PHYSICAL TRADING CAPACITY — a table, room-night, seat or ticket — with hospitality status vocabulary. THAT SCHEMA OWNS the slot with a NAMED PRACTITIONER for a SUBJECT OF CARE, with a clinical or procedure code, chart or patient reference, or practitioner-registration token. Discriminated by CARE ROLE versus SELLABLE CAPACITY. Neither may take the other on names-plus-times alone.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Q3 all-hands - agenda and timings.docx` — date, room, attendees, timings. THIS ROW OWNS a reservation only when sellable or bookable trading capacity is consumed against a status and usually a covers or room-night quantity for a guest-facing occasion. THAT ROW OWNS a CONVENING record — agenda, attendees, minutes, actions with owners — even when a meeting room was reserved. Discriminated by convening apparatus versus capacity-status apparatus. BOOKINGS-RESERVATIONS MUST NOT TAKE an internal all-hands pack; MEETING-RECORD MUST NOT TAKE a covers diary merely because it lists times and names.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Deposit request - Ashcroft wedding 06.06.26 - booking 4401.pdf` — amount, payment instructions, booking reference, occasion date. On ONE evidence item the rows mutex when the file is only a payment instrument with a merchant and an amount and no capacity-status apparatus — finance owns that receipt shape. THIS ROW OWNS the same bytes when the labelled slots are a reservation reference bound to covers or room-nights and a hold/confirmed status. They may also co-activate on DISJOINT evidence inside one packet (confirmation plus separate settlement statement); that join is recorded on file examples via also_schema and is not a licence to copy finance facts into this fieldless schema. Discriminated by whether capacity-and-status slots are present beside the money.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: a Saturday covers sheet that also carries a 'covers sold' total used later in an end-of-day pack. THIS ROW OWNS the reservation and status grid before and during service. THAT ROW OWNS tender-split takings, declared cash against expected, and over/short for a till session. Discriminated by tender-reconciliation structure versus reservation-status structure. Neither takes the other on a covers number alone.

falls_through_to.why: THE PRIMARY FALLTHROUGH FOR THE CUSTOMER-SIDE FALSE FRIEND, and the residual 00 names by the exact material: “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.” An isolated guest-addressed confirmation — including `Booking confirmation - Le Petit Jardin 14 Mar.pdf` — belongs here when this row does not fire.

Reached constantly by this row's genuine material when no accepted group is active: a PMS export full of guest names, phones, dietary notes and sometimes card-guarantee tokens. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The cautious outcome when SIDE is unresolved — a booking-shaped PDF that might be the operator's confirmation or the guest's download — or when OCR cannot read a photographed reservation book. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

Named as a must-consider residual; applies narrowly to a durable standalone booking-adjacent instrument with no cycle around it — a one-off venue-hire confirmation kept for its own sake with no diary beside it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The home for a single screenshotted diary tile or confirmation banner with no population and no recurring reference. “Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.” Positive screen-origin evidence is required; missing EXIF is not proof.

The safe outcome for a password-protected guest export or an unreadable PMS dump. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: THIS IS THE LEG THIS ROW PASSES MOST CLEARLY relative to stocktake and catalogue siblings. Almost every activating artefact names members of the public — guest identity, contact details, dietary and accessibility notes, celebration context, and sometimes payment-guarantee tokens. The posture is not merely inherited from the schema: isolated transactional booking records fall to Receipts and Confirmations, but operator population exports and requirement notes are Protected-Records-shaped by default and must not be dumped into cloud prompts. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” Guest names are never destination-eligible. Handling classes remain P7's; this row records only potentially_sensitive.
open_question: Four, recorded rather than smoothed. NJ-BR-1 (sharpest dimensional strain): because the trading occasion IS the booking, this row's recommended order is nearly the schema default with a specialised trailing function — thinner than guest-feedback's channel substitution. Alternatives: keep the row on detection and privacy alone (this pass); require a positive second dimension such as booking source/channel before the row is considered distinct; or fold operator booking recognition into the schema default and refuse this id. NJ-BR-2: whether booking SOURCE (OpenTable, Booking.com, phone, walk-in) should reuse guest-feedback's proposed `channel` key or remain unkeyed. This pass mints nothing and asks R1c to widen `channel` if both rows need it. NJ-BR-3: the moment a function hold becomes catering-contract or event-production — deposit confirmation versus signed function contract versus run sheet — is a packet progression, not a single-byte test; R1c should make all three rows say the same progression rule. NJ-BR-4: traveler lodging vouchers that a small B&B operator also files as their only PMS — holder operates AND stays nowhere else — may look like both sides at once; alternatives are Review Later, force operator-population evidence, or a Joseph ruling on dual-role corpora.
